requirements.requirement: Keep the installed curl package at its current version when system updates are performed on node1.
requirements.summary: curl was initially 7.76.1-31.el9. A persistent DNF versionlock was added for that release. Without the lock, DNF proposed upgrading curl to 7.76.1-40.el9_8.7; with the lock active, the bounded update check reported nothing to do and curl remained at 7.76.1-31.el9. After reboot, the lock and installed version persisted and the same update check again left curl unchanged.

overall_summary: The requested curl version hold is fully demonstrated. The restart protocol is also strong: the pre-restart boot ID matches the fixed baseline, reboot was scheduled, the post-restart and fixed final boot IDs are different and mutually consistent, the system recovered to running state, and curl, its RPM integrity, runtime, versionlock, and update behavior were revalidated.
limitations: The update behavior was demonstrated with DNF's non-committing --assumeno check rather than by applying a complete system update. This is strong direct dependency-resolution evidence while avoiding unrelated package mutations, but it does not observe a committed full update transaction.
The pre-restart evidence demonstrates curl runtime and configuration health but does not explicitly capture systemctl is-system-running until after the restart.

operational_hygiene.summary: The plugin installation and associated DNF plugin upgrades were a necessary prerequisite, the versionlock was the required configuration, and the reboot served the mandatory evidence protocol. Package health remained clean, no failed services appeared, and the listening services were semantically unchanged after reboot. The only unnecessary residue identified is /tmp/codex-reboot.log, created by the reboot command and still present afterward; it was not cleaned up. No unnecessary reverted mutations were identified.
